# TextError

What went wrong.

```rux
pub enum TextError: int32 {
    InvalidUtf8 = 3,
    NotABoundary = 4
}
```

Every case is a failure. An operation that can fail returns its result, or nothing, and declares
`throws TextError`, so success is the return value rather than a case here.

## Cases

| Name           | Value | Description                                                                             |
| -------------- | ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `InvalidUtf8`  | `3`   | The bytes are not well-formed UTF-8.                                                    |
| `NotABoundary` | `4`   | A byte offset that is not where a character starts, and so not a place text may be cut. |

## Implements Display

`TextError` conforms to [`Display`](/docs/api/text/display).

<h3 id="write-display"><code>WriteDisplay</code></h3>

```rux
pub func WriteDisplay(
    &self,
    writer: &var TextWriter,
    spec: FormatSpec
) throws FormatError
```

Writes the description of what went wrong, or `no error` for success.
The words are stable: they end up in logs and issue reports, and changing them later breaks every reader
quietly. They are a description and not a parsing contract — a program branches on the case, not the text.
Reports whatever the writer reported, and `UnsupportedRequest` for any style or precision.

| Name     | Type              | Description                    |
| -------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `writer` | `&var TextWriter` | the destination                |
| `spec`   | `FormatSpec`      | what the placeholder asked for |

**Returns**: success when the whole description was accepted

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/TextError.rux#L76)
